title: OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 on macOS for every R&D entry point, said honestly, and memory retire kept on DCLab's page
request: Owner: continue (after 'what else remains'): the same OpenMP freeze could hit R&D's server started by hand; re-sync DCLab Code after R&D's new commits; clear the stuck job.
plan: set the default where every R&D entry point starts (dclab_rnd/__init__.py), macOS only, a person's value wins
test it in a fresh interpreter with the variable removed
sync-check DCLab Code and decide what the new route means
leave the stuck intern job to R&D's worker recovery

decisions.decision: put the default in dclab_rnd/__init__.py, macOS only
decisions.why: it is the one module every entry point imports before PyTorch or LightGBM (the reviewer confirmed for mcp_server, worker, uvicorn via make notebook and scripts/dev.py); Linux runs a single OpenMP runtime

decisions.decision: keep the guard but word it as unproven
decisions.why: the reviewer measured that LightGBM's explicit n_jobs=4 ignores OMP_NUM_THREADS, and the cure rests on one restart; predictions are identical with one thread, so it is harmless

decisions.decision: do not change LightGBM's n_jobs now
decisions.why: no evidence yet that LightGBM's team is the one that hung; it is the next step if a freeze comes back

decisions.decision: add memory/{id}/retire to the never-relayed rule
decisions.why: retiring a memory changes what every agent reads; like review and correct it is the person's, on DCLab's page

change: R&D: dclab_rnd/__init__.py, tests/test_openmp_default.py. dclab-code 32c1cab (retire never relayed, lock at R&D 55af168c), and the reworded OpenMP comment.

findings.defect: the change claimed 'one OpenMP thread' but LightGBM still runs several
findings.scenario: with OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, LightGBM n_jobs=4 measured CPU/wall 2.4 (default n_jobs 3.2); XGBoost hist 0.98, HistGradientBoosting 0.99, torch 1 thread
findings.cause: dclab_rnd/expansion/runner.py builds LightGBM with an explicit n_jobs, which overrides the variable
findings.fix: comments in both repos now say what it limits and that the cure is one run; the next step is written down
findings.test: tests/test_openmp_default.py (fails on the old file, passes under run_parallel.py)

findings.scenario: slower single-thread XGBoost/HGB fits: engine.py skips refits over REFIT_SECONDS sooner; search.py fits fewer trials before its deadline

findings.defect: R&D added a person's memory route the chat must not send
findings.scenario: sync-check after R&D 55af168c: personWrites added POST /api/memory/{item_id}/retire

measurements.name: OpenMP default
measurements.gate: fresh interpreter: '1' on macOS when unset; a person's value wins

measurements.name: DCLab Code sync
measurements.gate: sync-check passes against R&D's latest commit
measurements.result: in sync with R&D, 18/18 agents reached

outcome: R&D's own servers on macOS get the same OpenMP setting DCLab Code gives them, with its limits written down; DCLab Code keeps retiring a memory as the person's act.
lessons: An environment variable is a request, not a rule: a library given an explicit thread count ignores it. Measure what it changes.
When a fix rests on one run, say so in the code.
risks: A LightGBM-heavy stage could still freeze if LightGBM's own thread team is the cause.
On macOS, search and refit decisions that depend on time can differ from Linux and CI.
